"""Consolidated accounting observations; calculation remains in product_billing.

Source identities are deliberately namespaced. Two observations are not one
charge merely because they have the same ID, amount, or timestamp. The existing
reconciler, rather than this storage layer, decides which charges overlap.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import JSON, BigInteger, Boolean, CheckConstraint, Index, Integer, String, Text, text
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from .models import Base


class BillingRecord(Base):
    __tablename__ = "moyai_billing_records"

    source: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), primary_key=True)
    source_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, primary_key=True)
    created_at: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    finished_at: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    model: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    actor_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    cost_usd: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    cost_source: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    input_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    output_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    total_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    cache_read_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    cache_write_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)

    # Native request identity and metadata. Legacy rows leave these null.
    request_key: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), unique=True, nullable=True)
    session_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(36), nullable=True)
    turn_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(36), nullable=True)
    response_model: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(200), nullable=True)
    provider: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(30), nullable=True)
    provider_request_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(200), nullable=True)
    response_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(200), nullable=True)
    provider_scope: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=True)
    receipt_key: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), unique=True, nullable=True)
    provider_timestamp: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(40), nullable=True)
    reasoning_tokens: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    cost_status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=True)
    coverage_error: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(50), nullable=True)

    # Historical metadata remains available to the unchanged recovery policy.
    legacy_run_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    message_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    key_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    gateway_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    gateway_scope: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    cost_receipt_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    cost_next_attempt_at: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    cost_recovery_attempts: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(BigInteger, nullable=True)
    cost_recovery_error: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)

    __table_args__ = (
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_source_time", "source", "created_at"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_gateway", "source", "gateway_id"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_provider", "source", "provider_request_id"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_actor_time", "actor_id", "created_at"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_session", "session_id"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_turn", "turn_id"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_legacy_run", "legacy_run_id"),
        Index("ix_moyai_billing_records_legacy_recovery", "key_hash", "gateway_scope", "cost_next_attempt_at"),
        Index(
            "ix_moyai_billing_records_legacy_receipt", "gateway_scope", "key_hash", "cost_receipt_id",
            unique=True, postgresql_where=text("source='legacy' AND cost_receipt_id<>''"),
            sqlite_where=text("source='legacy' AND cost_receipt_id<>''"),
        ),
        CheckConstraint("source IN ('legacy','native')", name="moyai_billing_source"),
    )


class BillingStorageState(Base):
    __tablename__ = "moyai_billing_storage"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    source_schema: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text)
    native_schema: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text)
    phase: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20))
    legacy_cursor: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    native_cursor: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    legacy_done: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean)
    native_done: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean)
    view_manifest: Mapped[dict[str, Any] | None] = mapped_column(
        JSON().with_variant(JSONB, "postgresql"), nullable=True,
    )


LEGACY_COLUMNS = {
    "id": "source_id", "run_id": "legacy_run_id", "user_id": "actor_id", "cost": "cost_usd",
    "prompt_tokens": "input_tokens", "completion_tokens": "output_tokens",
    "cache_read_input_tokens": "cache_read_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens": "cache_write_tokens",
}


def storage_column(source: str, field: str) -> str:
    if field == "id":
        return "source_id"
    return LEGACY_COLUMNS.get(field, field) if source == "legacy" else field

from __future__ import annotations

@pytest_asyncio.fixture
async def cutover(billing):
    ctx = billing
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text("ALTER TABLE moyai.model_requests DROP COLUMN private_payload, DROP COLUMN api_key"))
        await db.execute(text("CREATE TABLE moyai.runs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY)"))
        await db.execute(text("INSERT INTO moyai.runs VALUES('historical-child')"))
        await db.execute(text(
            "ALTER TABLE moyai.model_requests ADD FOREIGN KEY(run_id) REFERENCES moyai.runs(id)"
        ))
        await db.execute(text("CREATE TABLE moyai.schema_state(id integer PRIMARY KEY,revision integer,dirty integer)"))
        await db.execute(text("INSERT INTO moyai.schema_state VALUES(1,22,0)"))
    await seed(ctx, old=[old_row()], new=[new_row(provider_request_id="distinct")])
    await prepare(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    await finish_backfill(ctx)
    return ctx


async def test_cutover_leaves_one_store_and_exact_reports(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    before = await projection(ctx)
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    assert await projection(ctx) == before
    assert (await status(ctx.engine, ctx.storage))["physical_billing_stores"] == 1
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        for source in ("legacy", "native"):
            assert await db.scalar(text("SELECT relkind::text FROM pg_class WHERE oid=CAST(:name AS regclass)"), {
                "name": ctx.storage.source_table(source),
            }) == "v"
        assert await db.scalar(text("SELECT relkind::text FROM pg_class WHERE oid=CAST(:name AS regclass)"), {
            "name": ctx.storage.ledger,
        }) == "r"
        assert await db.scalar(text(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace "
            "WHERE n.nspname=:schema AND p.proname LIKE 'moyai_billing_mirror_%'"
        ), {"schema": ctx.storage.native_schema}) == 0
        await verify_consolidated(db, ctx.storage)
    await verify_product_schema(ctx.engine, schema=ctx.storage.native_schema)
    with pytest.raises(BillingStorageError, match="physically consolidated"):
        await rollback(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)


async def test_guard_runs_inside_exclusive_ownership_before_any_table_retirement(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    before = await projection(ctx)
    called = []

    async def reject(connection):
        pid = await connection.scalar(text("SELECT pg_backend_pid()"))
        held = (await connection.execute(text(
            "SELECT pid,mode FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype='advisory' AND classid=726940 "
            "AND objid='moyai'::regnamespace::oid AND objsubid=2 AND granted"
        ))).all()
        assert held == [(pid, "ExclusiveLock")]
        assert await connection.scalar(text(
            "SELECT relkind::text FROM pg_class WHERE oid='moyai.model_requests'::regclass"
        )) == "r"
        called.append(pid)
        raise BillingStorageError("Synthetic release guard refused cutover.")

    with pytest.raises(BillingStorageError, match="release guard"):
        await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage, before_consolidate=reject)
    assert len(called) == 1 and (await status(ctx.engine, ctx.storage))["phase"] == "shadow"
    assert await projection(ctx) == before
    comparison = await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    assert comparison == {
        "legacy": {"source_rows": 1, "mismatches": 0, "extra_rows": 0},
        "native": {"source_rows": 1, "mismatches": 0, "extra_rows": 0},
    }


async def test_native_insert_upsert_locks_and_recovery_updates_use_the_same_row(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    sessions = async_sessionmaker(ctx.native, expire_on_commit=False)
    value = new_row(id="later-native", request_key="later-key", cost_usd=None, cost_status="missing")
    statement = insert(InferenceUsage).values(**value)
    async with sessions.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(statement.on_conflict_do_update(
            index_elements=["request_key"], set_={
                "cost_usd": func.coalesce(InferenceUsage.cost_usd, statement.excluded.cost_usd),
            },
        ))
    async with sessions.begin() as db:
        row = await db.get(InferenceUsage, value["id"], with_for_update=True)
        row.cost_usd, row.cost_status, row.cost_source = "0.20000001", "actual", "gateway_recovery"
    async with sessions.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(statement.on_conflict_do_update(
            index_elements=["request_key"], set_={
                "cost_usd": func.coalesce(InferenceUsage.cost_usd, statement.excluded.cost_usd),
            },
        ))
        assert (await db.get(InferenceUsage, value["id"])).cost_usd == "0.20000001"
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        assert await db.scalar(text(
            f"SELECT cost_usd FROM {ctx.storage.ledger} WHERE source='native' AND source_id='later-native'"
        )) == "0.20000001"
        assert await db.scalar(text(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {ctx.storage.ledger}")) == 3


async def test_legacy_write_and_parent_delete_constraints_survive(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    await seed(ctx, old=[old_row(id="later-legacy", cost=None)])
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        assert (await db.execute(text(
            "UPDATE moyai.model_requests SET cost='1.23456789',cost_source='gateway_recovery' "
            "WHERE id='later-legacy'"
        ))).rowcount == 1
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        assert await db.scalar(text(
            f"SELECT cost_usd FROM {ctx.storage.ledger} WHERE source='legacy' AND source_id='later-legacy'"
        )) == "1.23456789"
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError):
        async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
            await db.execute(text("DELETE FROM moyai.runs WHERE id='historical-child'"))
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError):
        async with ctx.native.begin() as db:
            await db.execute(text("UPDATE moyai_inference_usage SET actor_id=NULL"))
    with pytest.raises(DBAPIError) as denied:
        async with ctx.native.begin() as db:
            await db.execute(text("UPDATE moyai_inference_usage SET source='legacy'"))
    assert getattr(denied.value.orig, "sqlstate", None) == "44000"


async def test_runtime_owner_prevents_physical_cutover(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as owner:
        await owner.execute(text(
            "SELECT pg_advisory_lock_shared(726940,'moyai'::regnamespace::oid::int)"
        ))
        try:
            with pytest.raises(BillingStorageError, match="stop all Moyai"):
                await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
        finally:
            await owner.execute(text(
                "SELECT pg_advisory_unlock_shared(726940,'moyai'::regnamespace::oid::int)"
            ))
    assert (await status(ctx.engine, ctx.storage))["phase"] == "shadow"


async def test_unknown_source_columns_stop_retirement_without_data_loss(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text("ALTER TABLE moyai.model_requests ADD COLUMN custom_evidence text"))
    with pytest.raises(BillingStorageError, match="unmapped columns"):
        await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:

            "SELECT relkind::text FROM pg_class WHERE oid='moyai.model_requests'::regclass"

async def test_existing_view_grantee_cannot_read_the_other_source_or_base_table(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    role = "billing_reader_" + uuid4().hex
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text(f'CREATE ROLE "{role}"'))
        await db.execute(text(f'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA moyai TO "{role}"'))
        await db.execute(text(f'GRANT SELECT ON moyai.model_requests TO "{role}"'))
    try:
        await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
        async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
            await db.execute(text(f'SET LOCAL ROLE "{role}"'))
            assert await db.scalar(text("SELECT count(*) FROM moyai.model_requests")) == 1
        with pytest.raises(ProgrammingError):
            async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
                await db.execute(text(f'SET LOCAL ROLE "{role}"'))
                await db.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {ctx.storage.ledger}"))
    finally:
        async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
            await db.execute(text(f'DROP OWNED BY "{role}"'))
            await db.execute(text(f'DROP ROLE "{role}"'))


async def test_native_view_definition_drift_is_rejected(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text(f"ALTER VIEW {ctx.storage.source_table('native')} RESET(security_barrier)"))
    with pytest.raises(BillingStorageError, match="differs"):

async def test_scoped_legacy_receipt_uniqueness_and_cross_source_ids_survive(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text(
            "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX original_receipt ON moyai.model_requests"
            "(gateway_scope,key_hash,cost_receipt_id) WHERE cost_receipt_id<>''"
        ))
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    # An existing native ID remains a valid, separate historical source ID.
    await seed(ctx, old=[old_row(id="native-observation", cost_receipt_id="receipt")])
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError):
        await seed(ctx, old=[old_row(id="duplicate-receipt", cost_receipt_id="receipt")])
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        assert await db.scalar(text(
            f"SELECT count(*) FROM {ctx.storage.ledger} WHERE source_id='native-observation'"
        )) == 2


async def test_long_historical_identity_survives_without_relaxing_native_identity_limits(cutover):
    ctx = cutover
    identity = "historical:" + "u" * 600
    await seed(ctx, old=[old_row(id="long-history", user_id=identity)])
    await consolidate(ctx.engine, ctx.storage)
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        assert await db.scalar(text(
            "SELECT user_id FROM moyai.model_requests WHERE id='long-history'"
        )) == identity
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError) as rejected:
        await seed(ctx, new=[new_row(id="long-native", request_key="long-native-key", actor_id=identity)])
    assert getattr(rejected.value.orig, "sqlstate", None) == "23514"

async def seed(ctx, *, old=(), new=()):
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        for row in old:
            values = {name: value for name, value in row.items() if name != "root_id"}
            await db.execute(text(
                f"INSERT INTO moyai.model_requests ({','.join(values)}) "
                f"VALUES ({','.join(':' + name for name in values)})"
            ), values)
    async with ctx.native.begin() as db:
        for row in new:
            await db.execute(insert(InferenceUsage).values(**row))


async def finish_backfill(ctx, size=1):
    for source in ("legacy", "native"):
        while not await backfill_batch(ctx.engine, ctx.storage, source, batch_size=size):
            pass


async def projection(ctx):
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as old_conn, ctx.native.connect() as new_conn:
        await old_conn.execute(text("SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY"))
        await new_conn.execute(text("SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY"))
        selected = await active_storage(
            new_conn, source_schema=ctx.storage.source_schema, native_schema=ctx.storage.native_schema,
        )
        old = BillingReader(old_conn, schema=ctx.storage.source_schema, storage=selected, billing_connection=new_conn)
        new = BillingReader(new_conn, schema=ctx.storage.native_schema, storage=selected)
        return await read_product_billing(
            old, new, PERIOD, rules=LegacyBillingRules.from_product(), mappings=MAPPINGS,
            policy=RecoveryPolicy(True, SCOPE), clock=CLOCK,
        )


async def test_family_lookup_expands_recursive_history_once_and_preserves_roots(billing):
    ctx = billing
    async with ctx.engine.begin() as db:
        await db.execute(text("DROP TABLE moyai.run_roots"))
        await db.execute(text("CREATE TABLE moyai.runs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,parent_run_id TEXT)"))
        await db.execute(text("""
            INSERT INTO moyai.runs
            SELECT 'root-' || n,'' FROM generate_series(1,501) n
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 'child-' || n,'root-' || n FROM generate_series(1,501) n
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 'leaf-' || n,'child-' || n FROM generate_series(1,501) n
        """))
        await db.execute(text("""
            INSERT INTO moyai.runs VALUES
            ('orphan','missing'),('cycle-a','cycle-b'),('cycle-b','cycle-a')
        """))
        await db.execute(text("""
            CREATE VIEW moyai.run_roots AS
            WITH RECURSIVE ancestry(ancestor_id,run_id) AS (
                SELECT id,id FROM moyai.runs UNION
                SELECT ancestry.ancestor_id,r.id FROM ancestry
                JOIN moyai.runs r ON r.parent_run_id=ancestry.run_id
            )
            SELECT ancestry.run_id,r.id AS root_id FROM ancestry
            JOIN moyai.runs r ON r.id=ancestry.ancestor_id WHERE r.parent_run_id=''
        """))
    queries = []

    def observe(_conn, _cursor, statement, _parameters, _context, _many):
        if "FROM moyai.run_roots" in statement:
            queries.append(statement)

    event.listen(ctx.engine.sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", observe)
    try:
        async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
            reader = BillingReader(db, schema="moyai")
            assert await reader.families([]) == {}
            assert not queries
            wanted = [f"leaf-{n}" for n in range(1, 502)] + ["leaf-1", "orphan", "cycle-a", "missing"]
            result = await reader.families(wanted)
            assert result == {f"leaf-{n}": f"root-{n}" for n in range(1, 502)}
            assert len(queries) == 1
            assert "= ANY" in queries[0]
            with pytest.raises(BillingReadError, match="too_many_session_family_records"):
                await BillingReader(db, schema="moyai", max_records=2).families(wanted)
    finally:
        event.remove(ctx.engine.sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", observe)


async def test_accounting_queries_exceed_old_cap_without_changing_pool_defaults(billing):
    ctx = billing
    service = ProductBillingService(
        None, ctx.engine, ctx.native, schema=ctx.storage.source_schema,
        native_schema=ctx.storage.native_schema,
    )
    async with ctx.engine.connect() as db:
        await db.execute(text("SET statement_timeout='5s'"))
        await db.execute(text("SET jit=on"))
        await db.commit()
    async with service._report_read(), service._reader(ctx.engine, ctx.storage.source_schema) as reader:
        assert await reader.connection.scalar(text("SHOW statement_timeout")) == "0"
        assert await reader.connection.scalar(text("SHOW jit")) == "off"
        assert await reader.connection.scalar(text("SHOW transaction_read_only")) == "on"

Search & Fetch

The Search API and the Fetch API give agents and RAG applications access to live web content:

Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. It is powered by DeepSeek's in-house search engine.

Fetch API retrieves a single web page and returns its content as Markdown.

Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.

The base URL is https://api.deepseek.com:

APIEndpoint
SearchPOST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search
FetchPOST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch

See the Search API Reference and Fetch API Reference for the complete request and response schemas.

Authentication​

Send your API key and the JSON content type in the request headers:

HeaderRequiredValue
AuthorizationYesBearer <DeepSeek API Key>
Content-TypeYesapplication/json

Search API​

Request​

curl https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "DeepSeek V4 release",
    "count": 5,
    "need_content": true
  }'

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search",
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>",
    },
    json={
        "query": "DeepSeek V4 release",
        "count": 5,
        "need_content": True,
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    print(result["title"], result["url"])
    print(result["summary"])

Request fields:

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
querystringYes-The search query must contain 1 to 128 Unicode characters, cannot be all whitespace, and supports the query operators listed below.
countintegerNo10The number of results to return, between 1 and 50.
ori_questionstringNo-The user's original question that triggered the search, between 1 and 128 characters, to improve query understanding, with null treated as not provided.
localizationstringNo""An optional IP address used to localize search results.
need_contentbooleanNofalseWhether to return page content in content, which is always an empty string when false.

Unknown fields in the request body are ignored.

Query Operators​

The query is forwarded with its search syntax intact. The examples below combine operators with a search term; you can combine multiple operators in one query.

OperatorExampleDescription
site:DeepSeek site:github.comRestrict results to the given site, and to target multiple sites, separate the site: clauses with spaces and join them with OR, for example DeepSeek site:github.com OR site:huggingface.co.
-site:DeepSeek -site:example.comExclude the given site, and separate multiple sites with spaces.
-DeepSeek -advertisementExclude pages containing the term, and separate multiple terms with spaces.
-"..."DeepSeek -"release notes"Exclude pages containing the exact phrase, which can contain spaces, and separate multiple phrases with spaces.
"..."DeepSeek "exact phrase"Match an exact phrase, and separate multiple phrases with spaces.
lang:DeepSeek lang:zh,enRestrict results to the given language codes, separating multiple codes with commas, for example lang:zh,en.
after:DeepSeek after:2025 or DeepSeek after:2025-01-01Restrict results to pages published after a date.
before:DeepSeek before:2026 or DeepSeek before:2026-06-01Restrict results to pages published before a date.

For example:

{
  "query": "DeepSeek site:github.com OR site:huggingface.co lang:en after:2025",
  "count": 10
}

Response​

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with a results array. A normal search with no matches returns an empty array.

{
  "results": [
    {
      "rerank_score": 2.4,
      "title": "DeepSeek V4 model released",
      "url": "https://example.com/deepseek-v4",
      "snippet": "DeepSeek V4 is now available, with tool calling and long-context support.",
      "summary": "DeepSeek has released the V4 model. The release adds improved tool calling and long-context support for agent workflows.",
      "content": "DeepSeek V4 is now generally available...",
      "site_name": "Example News",
      "site_icon": "https://example.com/favicon.ico",
      "date": "2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00",
      "authority": 3
    }
  ]
}

Each item in results contains:

FieldTypeDescription
rerank_scorenumberA relevance score from 0 to 3 that combines signals such as relevance, authority, and freshness, with scores of 1.5 or above considered high-quality results.
titlestringThe title of the result.
urlstringThe URL of the result.
snippetstringA short summary related to the query, typically 100 to 200 characters, intended for display in a UI.
summarystringA long summary related to the query, typically 600 to 800 characters, intended to be read by a model.
contentstringThe page content, which is empty when need_content is false or when the content is unavailable.
site_namestring or nullThe name of the site, or null when unavailable.
site_iconstring or nullThe URL of the site icon, or null when unavailable.
datestring or nullThe publication time in UTC, formatted as RFC 3339, or null when unknown.
authorityintegerThe authority tier of the page, 0 to 4 (-1 means unknown), with values of 3 or above indicating highly authoritative sources.

Fetch API​

Request​

curl https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://example.com/article"
  }'

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch",
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>",
    },
    json={"url": "https://example.com/article"},
)
response.raise_for_status()

page = response.json()
print(page["title"])
print(page["content"])

Request fields:

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
urlstringYesThe page URL to fetch, which must be at most 8192 characters, an HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host, and must not contain a username or password.

Response​

{
  "title": "Example article",
  "content": "# Example article\n\nArticle content."
}

FieldTypeDescription
titlestringThe title of the page, empty when the title is unavailable.
contentstringThe fetched page content as Markdown text.

Fetching is subject to the target site's availability and access policies.

Errors​

Errors follow the OpenAI-compatible error format. The param field is always null.

{
  "error": {
    "message": "'count' must be between 1 and 50",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}

HTTP StatusDescription
400The request headers or body are invalid, including malformed JSON or an invalid field value.
401The API key is missing or invalid.
402The account has insufficient balance.
403The Fetch request was rejected by the security policy.
404Fetch could not retrieve usable page content, for example due to an unavailable URL, a URL blocked by site policy, an error from the target site, an unsupported content type, or a page with no extractable Markdown content.
408Reading the request body timed out.
413The request body is too large.
429The Search or Fetch QPS limit was exceeded.
500An internal server error occurred.
504A downstream request timed out.

Search and Fetch are read-only. For HTTP 408, 429, or 5xx errors, wait and retry. For HTTP 402, top up your account before retrying. Do not retry other 4xx errors without changing the request.

Billing​

Search and Fetch are billed per successful request, not by tokens or by the number of returned results:

APIUnitPrice
SearchPer 1,000 successful requests$0.75
FetchPer 1,000 successful requests$0.75

A request is billable only when it returns HTTP 200 and produces a result (Search must return a non-empty results array, and Fetch must return page content). Failed requests, empty search results, and timeouts are not billed. count only controls how many results are returned and does not affect the per-request price.

Note: when you use the DeepSeek API through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, or Codex, server-side tool calls already hit the Search and Fetch APIs. These calls are currently free of charge; per-request billing starts at 00:00 Beijing time on November 1, 2026.

Rate Limits​

For each account, Search and Fetch are limited independently, and traffic to one does not consume the other's quota:

APIQPS Limit
Search5
Fetch5

The QPS (requests per second) limits are calculated at the account level, regardless of which API key is used, and are separate from the model concurrency limits. Requests above the account-level QPS limit receive HTTP 429. In addition to the account-level limit, Fetch is also subject to a per-domain QPS limit, and requests above that limit also receive HTTP 429.

# Consolidate the two spend tables into one store

The completed migration stores legacy and native billing records in one physical
table: `MOYAI_NATIVE_SCHEMA.moyai_billing_records`.

`model_requests` and `moyai_inference_usage` become ordinary PostgreSQL views over
that table. They contain no copies. Existing reads, inserts, updates, deletes,
native upserts and row locks go directly to the ledger through those names.
There are no mirroring triggers or old physical spend tables after the final
transaction commits. The small `moyai_billing_storage` table holds the migration
receipt and cursors, not a second copy of the spend records.

The migration preserves original IDs, exact recorded cost strings, nulls, statuses,
token counts and request metadata. Source IDs remain namespaced; equal IDs from
different engines do not prove duplicate charges. Existing calculations, charge
reconciliation, identity mappings and cost recovery remain unchanged. Operational
admission/turn tables retain their current purpose. This work does not recover
lost costs or change which history the native usage UI displays.

## Report reads

Usage, billing and CSV reports fetch accounting observations in batches of 2,000
within their read-only snapshots. The batch size is not a report limit: a date
range with more than 50,000 records includes every matching charge. Exact-ID
counterparts are still loaded before reconciliation and date attribution.
Request-detail pagination does not change aggregate totals.

Reconciliation reads the selected period once. Further rounds look up only new
aliases outside that period, keeping cross-date evidence without rereading the
same in-range rows. PostgreSQL batches up to 10,000 counterpart identities and
uses array parameters for admission lookups. All retained evidence belongs to
one report's snapshots; subsequent requests read current costs and permissions.

Reconciliation retains the report's evidence in memory; batching bounds the
database fetch buffer, not total report memory. PostgreSQL resolves all requested
historical session families with one array-bound query, so the recursive ancestry
view is expanded once rather than once per 200 sessions.

Accounting reports have no fixed execution deadline. Billing read transactions
disable the inherited five-second PostgreSQL statement timeout and JIT compilation;
those settings revert when the transaction ends. Caller cancellation still
releases readers. The previous fixed 15-second report and five-second statement
limits no longer apply to these billing reads. Connection-pool acquisition,
authentication and other application queries retain their own limits.

Database timeouts return a distinct message suggesting a retry. Server logs
contain phase timings and the exception type, without query text, parameters,
account IDs or credentials. The reconciliation-round limit and ambiguous-identity
checks still fail visibly without substituting partial totals. Explicit `max_records` bounds remain
available for diagnostic readers.

## Provision

Use the existing PostgreSQL connection and explicit distinct schemas:
`MOYAI_DATABASE_URL`, `MOYAI_DATABASE_SCHEMA`, and `MOYAI_NATIVE_SCHEMA`.
Standalone SQLite is unchanged.

Follow the existing maintenance and backup procedure. Canonical schema v22
recognizes the completed compatibility view during future migrations. Native
schema v15 adds the shared ledger and receipt tables while preserving earlier
native migration receipts.

```sh
python -m app.schema_migrations --apply
python -m moyai.product_start provision --apply
```

Normal application startup never copies history or retires tables.

## Copy while existing writers continue

```sh
python -m moyai.billing_storage prepare --apply
python -m moyai.billing_storage backfill --apply --batch-size 1000 --max-batches 100
python -m moyai.billing_storage status
```

During this temporary stage, PostgreSQL triggers mirror source changes into the
new table in the original write transaction. Both old tables remain authoritative
until physical cutover. Backfill commits a bounded batch and its cursor together.
Repeat it until both completion flags are true. Source-row locks prevent
delete/copy races, and a copied historical row cannot overwrite a newer mirrored
cost update. Inserts behind the cursor are captured by the temporary mirrors.

Commands use a five-second lock timeout and sixty-second statement timeout.
Timed-out batches do not advance their committed cursor and can be retried.

Optionally compare the new reporting path before physical cutover:

```sh
python -m moyai.billing_storage activate --apply
```

This validates every stored accounting field and switches the product billing
APIs and CSV exports. `activate` alone is not the completed consolidation.
Before physical cutover, `rollback --apply` can switch reads back while both
original tables remain current.

## Complete physical consolidation

Managed deployment procedures are maintained in a private repository.

For an independently coordinated installation, drain and stop all Moyai runtime
owners, then run the same installed migration command:

```sh
python -m moyai.billing_storage consolidate --apply
python -m moyai.billing_storage status
```

The command requires exclusive canonical runtime ownership and locks both source
tables. In one transaction it:

1. Verifies both backfills and the temporary mirrors, with no missing, extra or
   different records.
2. Preserves source nullability/length constraints, native unique request and
   receipt keys, the legacy run foreign key, supported indexes and source defaults.
3. Drops the two original tables with `RESTRICT` and creates automatically
   updatable, source-filtered views under their original names. The views use
   `CHECK OPTION` and a security barrier; existing data-access grants are retained
   without granting callers direct access to the whole ledger.
4. Removes the mirror functions and records the completed physical layout.

Unknown source columns, custom RLS, unsupported constraints/triggers, changed
ownership or dependent objects stop the transaction. Nothing is retired on a
failed comparison or failed DDL statement. The command never uses `DROP CASCADE`.
Custom database extensions must be reviewed and mapped before retirement.

Successful status is `phase: consolidated` and `physical_billing_stores: 1`.
Restart the updated application through the normal deployment workflow. Native
startup verifies the compatibility views and ledger constraints against the
cutover receipt. Re-running the physical cutover only verifies that receipt.

The original names continue to support the application's data operations; they
are no longer targets for physical-table DDL or `TRUNCATE`. Recovery updates
through either existing write interface modify the same ledger row. The billing
adapter reads the ledger directly, while user/session/privacy/admission lookups
continue using their owning tables.

## Rollback boundary

Before `consolidate`, use `rollback --apply` to select the original reporting path.
After `consolidate`, the two old stores no longer exist, so that read-only rollback
command refuses to imply that it can restore them. Restore the reviewed backup
or roll forward if a pre-cutover application/schema is required. Keep the backup
outside the active billing schema; the completed application maintains one store.

## One reporting API

`GET /api/settings/billing` is the canonical product billing and usage API.
Spend & usage calls it with `include_activity=true`; the response contains the
accounting report and an `activity` view for the dashboard. Both use the same
financial projection, including historical and native records. The activity
view reuses that projection rather than reading and summing billing again.
Its session, turn and PR measurements retain their native activity scope.

Each request uses one verified product-directory identity snapshot for accounting
and activity. Verified native product mirrors, including saved Slack links, use
the same actor namespace as historical charges; explicit configured mappings
take precedence. Equal raw IDs alone never join accounts. These report mappings
do not grant private-session access or establish missing charge provenance.

The existing `/api/settings/usage` URL remains a compatibility adapter for
clients expecting the older dashboard shape. `/api/admin/spend` and personal
`/api/spend` retain their existing scopes. They do not own separate spend
calculations. Standalone installations, which have no product history, keep
their native usage API.

Date and canonical user filters apply to the financial report. `model` selects
the recorded inference alias; `root_model` and `turn_status` select the saved
historical session or native turn cohort. The dashboard uses those latter two
filters. Daily, user and model CSV exports use the same canonical endpoint and
exact decimal amounts. `include_activity=true&format=csv&export=turns` exports
visible native turn details; it does not invent historical turn records.

Unknown amounts and unresolved identities remain explicit. Accounting totals
retain private usage, while request/session details and native turn exports
respect visibility. A failed financial read returns an error instead of falling
back to a native-only subtotal. Reporting is read-only and needs no additional
backfill or schema migration.

"""Explicit fresh-install schema preparation; no application or worker startup."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from collections.abc import Mapping
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

import psycopg
from psycopg import sql

from .deployment_checks import settings
from .deployment_config import InstallationError
from .postgres import create_engine


@asynccontextmanager
async def installation_lock(values: Mapping[str, str]):
    async with await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(
        values["MOYAI_DATABASE_URL"], connect_timeout=5, autocommit=True,
    ) as connection:
        cursor = await connection.execute(
            "SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended(%s,0))",
            ("moyai-install:" + values["MOYAI_NATIVE_DATABASE_SCHEMA"],),
        )
        row = await cursor.fetchone()
        if not row or not row[0]:
            raise InstallationError("Another installer owns this database namespace; wait for it to finish.")
        yield


def require_empty(values: Mapping[str, str]) -> None:
    schemas = [values["MOYAI_NATIVE_DATABASE_SCHEMA"]]
    if values["MOYAI_PRODUCT_MODE"] == "existing":
        schemas.append(values["MOYAI_DATABASE_SCHEMA"])
    with psycopg.connect(values["MOYAI_DATABASE_URL"], connect_timeout=5) as connection:
        for schema in schemas:
            populated = connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM pg_class WHERE relnamespace=to_regnamespace(%s) LIMIT 1", (schema,),
            ).fetchone()
            if populated:
                raise InstallationError(
                    "The target schema already contains data. Restore installation.json or use the reviewed migration procedure."
                )


async def provision(values: Mapping[str, str], *, fresh: bool) -> dict:
    from .product_config import load_product_config
    from .product_start import prepare_native_schema

    if values["MOYAI_PRODUCT_MODE"] == "existing":
        schema = values["MOYAI_DATABASE_SCHEMA"]
        if fresh:
            def create_schema() -> None:
                with psycopg.connect(values["MOYAI_DATABASE_URL"], connect_timeout=5) as connection:
                    connection.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {}").format(sql.Identifier(schema)))
            await asyncio.to_thread(create_schema)
        # Canonical migration retains historical settings semantics but runs
        # in this installation; no retired executor or second interpreter loads.
        migration = {
            **values, "MOYAI_CORE": "legacy", "MOYAI_RUNTIME_ROLE": "standalone",
            "MOYAI_DATABASE_INITIALIZE": str(fresh).lower(), "MOYAI_SCHEMA_MODE": "auto",
            "MOYAI_SEPARATE_BROKER": "false", "MOYAI_COORDINATOR_HANDOFF": "false",
        }
        completed = await asyncio.to_thread(
            subprocess.run, [sys.executable, "-m", "app.schema_migrations", "--apply"],
            env=migration, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, check=False,
        )
        if completed.returncode:
            raise InstallationError(
                "Product schema preparation failed. Keep services stopped and inspect the migration before retrying."
            )
        try:
            receipt = json.loads(completed.stdout)
            if receipt["status"] != "ready":
                raise ValueError
        except (ValueError, KeyError):
            raise InstallationError("Product schema preparation returned no verified receipt.") from None
        config = load_product_config(values)
        assert config is not None
        native = await prepare_native_schema(config, apply=True)
        return {"product": receipt, "native": native}

    from .database import Database
    from .product_schema import migrate_product_schema, verify_product_schema
    from .security import Security
    from .stores import NativeStores

    configured = settings(values)
    engine = create_engine(configured.sqlalchemy_url)
    stores = NativeStores(configured)
    try:
        revision = await migrate_product_schema(engine, schema=configured.database_schema)
        await stores.start(provision=True)
        if fresh:
            bootstrap = configured.model_copy(update={"native_schema_mode": "bootstrap"})
            database = Database(bootstrap, Security(bootstrap.master_key))
            try:
                await database.start()
            finally:
                await database.close()
        await verify_product_schema(engine, schema=configured.database_schema)
        return {"native": {"app_schema": revision, "harness_schema": "provisioned"}}
    finally:
        await stores.close()
        await engine.dispose()


async def verify(values: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict:
    from .product_config import load_product_config
    from .product_start import prepare_native_schema

    if values["MOYAI_PRODUCT_MODE"] == "existing":
        config = load_product_config(values)
        assert config is not None
        return await prepare_native_schema(config, apply=False)
    from .product_schema import verify_product_schema
    from .stores import NativeStores

    configured = settings(values)
    engine = create_engine(configured.sqlalchemy_url)
    stores = NativeStores(configured)
    try:
        await verify_product_schema(engine, schema=configured.database_schema)
        await stores.start()
        return {"app_schema": "verified", "harness_schema": "verified"}
    finally:
        await stores.close()
        await engine.dispose()

from test_application_boundaries import sign_in

])

async def test_failed_turn_needs_no_review_and_accepts_follow_up(runtime, active, actor, name, legacy):
    session, turn, prepared = active
    receipts = EffectReceipts(runtime.database)
    await receipts.reserve(prepared.scope, "failed-browser", name, {"url": "http://localhost:8840"})
    if name in {"browser_open", "browser_action"}:

    async with runtime.database.sessions() as db:

    await runtime.database.fail(turn.id, "The browser action failed.")

        assert response.status_code == 200
        view = response.json()

async def saved_action(runtime, run_id, *, name="shell", status="completed", output="README.md\nnative/", call_id="call"):
    await runtime.stores.steps.register_run(RunRecord(run_id=run_id, agent_name="moyai"))
    await runtime.stores.steps.append_event(StepEvent(
        run_id=run_id, kind="tool_call_started", step_index=1, tool_name=name, tool_call_id=call_id,
    ))
    messages = [
        ModelResponse(run_id="unrelated", parts=[ToolCallPart(name, {"private": "inherited input"}, tool_call_id=call_id)]),
        ModelRequest(parts=[ToolReturnPart(name, "inherited output", tool_call_id=call_id)]),
        ModelResponse(run_id=run_id, parts=[ThinkingPart("hidden reasoning"), ToolCallPart(name, {"command": "ls synthetic-gateway-secret"}, tool_call_id=call_id)]),
    ]
    if status != "running":
        await runtime.stores.steps.append_event(StepEvent(
            run_id=run_id, kind=f"tool_call_{status}", step_index=2, tool_name=name, tool_call_id=call_id,
            error="private provider metadata",
        ))
        result_type = RetryPromptPart if status == "failed" else ToolReturnPart
        messages.append(ModelRequest(parts=[result_type(tool_name=name, content=output, tool_call_id=call_id)]))
    await runtime.stores.steps.save_snapshot(ContinuableSnapshot(run_id=run_id, step_index=2, messages=messages))

        async with runtime.database.sessions.begin() as db:

async def test_canonical_check_is_fresh_and_does_not_hold_native_connection(runtime, actor):
    session = await runtime.database.create_session(actor, NewSession(visibility="private"))
    checked_out = 0
    checks = 0

    def checkout(*_):
        nonlocal checked_out
        checked_out += 1

    def checkin(*_):
        nonlocal checked_out
        checked_out -= 1

    async def canonical_check(_request):
        nonlocal checks
        assert checked_out == 0
        checks += 1
        if checks == 2:
            raise HTTPException(401, "Canonical authority changed.")

    identity = SimpleNamespace(require_request_current=canonical_check)
    event.listen(runtime.database.engine.sync_engine, "checkout", checkout)
    event.listen(runtime.database.engine.sync_engine, "checkin", checkin)
    try:
        await authorize_stream_viewer(runtime.database, identity, request(), actor, session.id, actor.id)
        with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as revoked:
            await authorize_stream_viewer(runtime.database, identity, request(), actor, session.id, actor.id)
        assert revoked.value.status_code == 401
        assert checks == 2
    finally:
        event.remove(runtime.database.engine.sync_engine, "checkout", checkout)
        event.remove(runtime.database.engine.sync_engine, "checkin", checkin)
